title: PIM-DL: Expanding the Applicability of Commodity DRAM-PIMs for Deep Learning via Algorithm-System Co-Optimization
problem: Commodity DRAM-PIMs are limited to element-wise and GEMV operations, which represent only a small portion of DNN execution time. Current systems still require powerful hosts to handle the majority of compute-heavy operators.
motivation: DRAM-based PIMs have gained commercial prominence, but their effectiveness for deep learning acceleration remains severely limited due to computational constraints.
method: The system co-designs both the algorithm and memory hardware together. Normally the specialized memory can only do simple per-number operations and basic matrix multiplication, leaving heavy lifting to the main processor. By tailoring algorithms to match what this memory does well, the system expands which calculation types it can handle, reducing main processor dependency.
key_novelty: Co-designing the algorithm and hardware system together lets the specialized memory handle more types of deep learning calculations.
contributions: Analysis of DRAM-PIM limitations in DNN workloads
Algorithm-system co-optimization framework for expanded operator support
Techniques to reduce host processor reliance for deep learning
Demonstration of commodity DRAM-PIMs for broader DNN operations
